questions.expl: Terrazzo flooring is characteristically made with marble chips of about 4 to 6 mm size.

questions.text: In flat roof of reinforced cement concrete, the recommended angle of slope, is
questions.expl: An RCC flat roof is given a slight slope of a few degrees to help drain rainwater.

questions.text: Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: The roof slabs of multi-storeyed buildings are constructed monolithically to carry the various floor loads
The beams of multi-storeyed buildings rest on girders and are the main load transferring members to the columns
The slab is spanned across the secondary beams provided between the main beams
questions.expl: All these statements correctly describe the structural framing of multi-storeyed buildings.

questions.text: The members which support covering material of a sloping roof, are
questions.expl: Rafters are the sloping members that ultimately support the roof covering material.

questions.text: Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: In a king post truss, principal rafter and tie beams are jointed together with a bridle joint
Joint between the principal rafter and the king post is made by making tenon and mortice respectively
Joint between strut and king post, is generally of mortice and tenon type
questions.expl: All these joint descriptions for a king post truss - bridle, tenon/mortice - are correct.

questions.text: The highest line of sloping roof, where two opposite slopes meet, is known as
questions.expl: The ridge is the highest line where two opposite roof slopes meet.

questions.text: The window which is provided in flat roof of a room, is known
questions.expl: A lantern window is the type provided on the flat roof of a room.

questions.text: In high mountainous region, the type of roof generally recommended for buildings, is
questions.expl: Gambrel-type roofs are generally recommended in mountainous regions for snow shedding and space.

questions.text: The ceiling height of a building is
options: Upto ceiling from the ground level
questions.expl: Ceiling height is measured as the vertical distance between the floor and the ceiling.

questions.text: The line of intersection of two surfaces of a sloping roof forming an internal angle less than 180 degrees, is known as
questions.expl: A valley is the internal intersection line of two roof slopes forming an angle less than 180 degrees.

questions.text: The art of bringing the floor to a true level surface by means of screeds, is called
questions.expl: Screeding is the process of levelling a floor surface using guide screeds.

questions.text: Glass flooring is generally preferred when
options: Light is to be transmitted from upper to lower floor
questions.expl: Glass flooring is chosen mainly to transmit light from an upper floor down to a lower one.

questions.text: Terrazzo flooring is obtained
options: By using marble chips aggregate in concrete
By spreading the marble chips over ordinary wet concrete
By mixing marble powder in ordinary concrete
questions.expl: Terrazzo flooring is made by using marble chips as the aggregate within a concrete topping.

questions.text: The biggest disadvantage of brick flooring is that
questions.expl: Brick flooring's main drawback is that bricks are water absorbent, making the floor prone to dampness.

questions.text: The form work from the underside of slabs, can be removed only after
questions.expl: Formwork under slab soffits, being load-bearing, is typically kept in place for about 7 days.

questions.text: The arrangement of supporting an existing structure by providing supports underneath, is known as
questions.expl: Underpinning is the technique of strengthening an existing foundation by providing supports underneath it.

questions.text: Dampness causes
questions.expl: Dampness creates favourable conditions for termite growth, among other deterioration effects listed.

questions.text: A temporary rigid structure having platforms to enable masons to work at different stages of a building, is known as
questions.expl: Scaffolding is the temporary structure with platforms that lets masons work at height during construction.

questions.text: The formwork including the props can be removed from beams, only after
questions.expl: Beam formwork along with its props is generally retained for about 14 days before removal.

questions.text: Pick up the consideration to be taken while designing a hospital from the following:
options: The operation theatre unit to be detached as it requires sterilized zone but near the ward for the patients and doctor
The mortuary should be detached from the main circulation with a postmortem room
Casualty unit should be provided a separate entrance
questions.expl: Hospital design must consider all these factors: OT zoning, mortuary separation, and a dedicated casualty entrance.

questions.text: The arrangement made to support and transfer structure temporarily, is known as
questions.expl: Shoring is the temporary arrangement used to support and transfer structural loads.

questions.text: Which of the following metal sheets is most effective in preventing dampness?
questions.expl: Copper, lead, and aluminium sheets are all effective metal damp-proofing materials.

questions.text: If the height of first storey of a building is 3.2 m and riser is 13 cm, the number of treads required is
questions.expl: Number of risers = 320/13 approx 24.6, taken as 24; treads = risers - 1, but per key the answer is 24.

questions.text: Soffit is the
questions.expl: Soffit refers to the underside (bottom surface) of a staircase.

questions.text: The vertical member fixed between steps and hand rail are known as
questions.expl: Balusters are the small vertical members supporting the handrail between steps.

questions.text: The vertical posts placed at the top and bottom ends of a flight supporting the hand rail are known as:
questions.expl: Newel posts are the larger vertical posts at the top and bottom of a flight that anchor the handrail.

questions.text: In any good staircase, the maximum and minimum pitch respectively should be:
questions.expl: A good staircase should have a pitch between 25 degrees minimum and 40 degrees maximum.

questions.text: Doglegged stairs are
questions.expl: Dog-legged stairs turn 180 degrees, making them a type of half-turn stair.

questions.text: Minimum width of landing should be
options: One fourth the width of stairs
questions.expl: A landing's minimum width should be at least equal to the width of the stair flight.

questions.text: Sum of tread and rise must lie between
questions.expl: The sum of tread and rise (T+R) is generally kept between 400 and 450 mm.

questions.text: The number of steps in a flight generally should not be less than
questions.expl: A flight of stairs should have a minimum of 3 steps for practicality and safety.

questions.text: The maximum number of steps in a flight should generally be restricted to
questions.expl: A single flight is generally limited to a maximum of 12 steps before a landing is needed.

questions.text: In a stair case design the product (Rise x Going) is approximately
questions.expl: The empirical rise-times-going product for comfortable stairs is approximately 425 cm2.

questions.text: Nosing is the outer projecting edge of a
questions.expl: Nosing is the rounded projecting edge of a tread beyond the riser face.

questions.text: Half turn stairs are the stairs which change their direction through
questions.expl: Half-turn stairs change direction by 180 degrees.

questions.text: The height between two floors is 3.00 m and riser is 150 mm, assuming two flights between the floors, the number of treads will be
questions.expl: Total risers = 3000/150 = 20; treads = risers - 1 = 19, but for two-flight configuration the key gives 18 treads.

questions.text: A stair should not have pitch more than
questions.expl: The maximum permissible pitch for a comfortable staircase is 40 degrees.

questions.text: Which of the following types of stairs is used for modern public buildings.
questions.expl: Bifurcated stairs, which split into two flights, are commonly used in modern public buildings for grandeur.

questions.text: The upper horizontal portion of the step where the foot is placed while ascending or descending is known as
questions.expl: The tread is the horizontal upper surface of a step where the foot is placed.

questions.text: The projected portion of the tread (which is usually rounded) beyond the face of the riser is
questions.expl: Nosing is the rounded projection of the tread extending beyond the riser face.

questions.text: A vertical member placed at the ends of flights connecting the hand rail is termed as
questions.expl: The newel post is the vertical member at flight ends connecting to the handrail.

questions.text: The normal tread length varies between
questions.expl: Normal tread length (going) generally ranges between 25 cm and 30 cm.

questions.text: A stair which changes its direction by 180 degrees is
questions.expl: A stair changing direction by exactly 180 degrees is termed a half-turn stair.

questions.text: Dog-legged stair is a
questions.expl: Dog-legged stairs are a form of half-turn stair with two flights and no well.

questions.text: How many treads would be there in a dog-legged stair connecting two floors with a height difference of 3.6 m? The rise of the steps is 15 cm
questions.expl: Number of risers = 360/15 = 24; treads = risers - 2 (one per flight/landing) = 22 per given key.

questions.text: The type of stairs with curved well formed between the two adjacent flights is known as
questions.expl: A geometric stair has a curved well formed between adjacent flights, without newel posts.

questions.text: Commonly required width of stair in residential building is
questions.expl: Residential building stairs are commonly designed with a width of about 0.9 m.

questions.text: Commonly required width of stair in public building is
questions.expl: Public buildings typically require stair widths of about 1.5 m to 2.5 m.

questions.text: The desirable rise of stair in residential and public buildings are respectively.
questions.expl: Desirable riser heights are 150-175 mm for residential and a lower 120-150 mm for public buildings.

questions.text: The going provided for stairs in residential and public buildings are usually respectively
questions.expl: Going is typically 250 mm for residential stairs and a larger 270 mm for public buildings.

questions.text: If R is rise and G is going of stairs, the empirical formula used to fix rise and going is 2R + G and it should be between
questions.expl: The empirical formula 2R+G should give a value between 550 mm and 650 mm for comfort.

questions.text: Headroom in a staircase should not be less than
questions.expl: Minimum headroom clearance in a staircase should not be less than 2.1 m.

questions.text: Minimum width of landing should be
options: One fourth the width of stairs
questions.expl: A landing should be at least as wide as the flight of stairs it serves.

questions.text: In any good staircase, the maximum and minimum pitch respectively should be
questions.expl: Good staircase design keeps the pitch between a minimum of 25 degrees and maximum of 40 degrees.

questions.text: Doglegged stairs are
questions.expl: Dog-legged stairs are classified as half-turn stairs, reversing direction by 180 degrees.

questions.text: While designing a stair, the product of rise and going is approximately kept equal to
questions.expl: The rise x going product is kept approximately equal to 420 (in cm2) for a comfortable stair.

questions.text: The angular steps used for changing direction of the stairs, are called
questions.expl: Winders are the tapered, angular steps used to change the direction of a staircase.

questions.text: The platform at the end of a series of steps, is known as
questions.expl: The flat resting platform at the end of a flight of steps is called a landing.

questions.text: Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: In dog-legged stairs, no space between its flights is provided
In open newel stair, a rectangular well is provided
In geometric stair, a curved shaped well between forward and backward flights, is provided
In geometrical stair, two quarter space landing is provided
questions.expl: A geometrical stair does not use two quarter-space landings; this makes the statement incorrect.

questions.text: The inclined support at the ends of treads and rises of a stair, is known as
questions.expl: The string is the inclined structural member supporting the ends of the treads and risers.

questions.text: If height of the first storey of a building is 3.2 m and riser is 13 cm, the number of treads required, is
questions.expl: Number of risers = 320/13 approx 24.6, taken as 24, matching the number of treads per the key.

questions.text: The minimum width of a stair in residential buildings, is
questions.expl: The minimum stair width in residential buildings is generally kept at about 85 cm.

questions.text: A stair should not have pitch more than
questions.expl: The maximum permissible pitch for a staircase is 40 degrees.

questions.text: The stone blocks approximately triangular in shape, used as steps, are known
questions.expl: Triangular stone blocks used as steps, with the underside filled solid, are called spandrel steps.

questions.text: The process of making the background rough, before plastering, is
questions.expl: Hacking is the process of roughening a smooth background surface to provide a key for plaster.

questions.text: The process of keeping concrete moist for a certain period after its finishing, is known as
questions.expl: Curing is the process of keeping concrete moist after finishing to aid proper hydration and strength gain.

questions.text: For effective drainage, the finished surface of flat roof should have a minimum slope of
questions.expl: A flat roof needs a minimum slope of about 1 in 20 for effective rainwater drainage.

questions.text: For plastering the exposed brick walls, the cement sand mortar should be
questions.expl: Exposed brick walls are generally plastered with cement-sand mortar in a 1:4 ratio.

questions.text: The local swelling of a finished plaster, is termed
questions.expl: Blistering refers to localized swelling that develops on a finished plaster surface.

questions.text: Pick up the correct statements from the following:
options: Cracks appear on the plastered surface in the form of hair cracks
In brick work, the efflorescence is removed by applying a solution of zinc sulphate and water
Excessive thermal variations in the backing or plaster causes the plaster to fall
questions.expl: All these statements correctly describe plaster defects: hair cracking, efflorescence removal, and thermal-induced falling.

questions.text: The type of pointing in which upper side of mortar joints is kept about 12 mm inside the face of the masonry and bottom is kept flushed with face of wall, is
questions.expl: Struck pointing has the top set back about 12 mm while the bottom stays flush with the wall face.

questions.text: The type of pointing in which a V-shaped projection outside the wall surface, is provided, is called
questions.expl: Weather pointing forms a V-shaped projection sloped to shed rainwater away from the joint.

questions.text: Dado is usually provided in
questions.expl: Dado, a protective wall finish up to a certain height, is usually provided in bathrooms.

questions.text: In horizontal D.P.C. thickness of cement concrete (1:2:4) is
questions.expl: Horizontal DPC in 1:2:4 cement concrete is generally laid about 4 cm thick.

questions.text: Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: D.P.C. should be of good impervious material
D.P.C. may be horizontal or vertical
questions.expl: DPC must be continuous, impervious, and can be provided horizontally or vertically - all correct.

questions.text: Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: The first coat of stucco plaster is called scratch coat
The second coat of stucco plaster is called brown coat
The third coat of stucco plaster is called white coat
questions.expl: Stucco plaster application uses these three named coats: scratch, brown, and white/finish coat.

questions.text: The X-ray rooms are plastered with
questions.expl: Barium plaster is used in X-ray rooms because it helps block radiation.

questions.text: The process of working a float for the finishing coat, is known
questions.expl: Floating is the process of using a float tool to work and finish the final plaster coat.

questions.text: The portion of the wall between the facing and backing of the wall is called
questions.expl: Hearting is the inner core portion of a wall lying between its facing and backing.

questions.text: A groove provided on the underside of projecting elements such as cornices, copings such that rain water can be discharged clear of the wall surface is called
questions.expl: Throating is a groove under a projection that drips rainwater clear of the wall face.

questions.text: The tool used by the masons to check the verticality of walls is
questions.expl: A plumb bob is used by masons to check that a wall is being built truly vertical.

questions.text: A junction at which two walls meet at an angle other than 90 degrees is called
questions.expl: A squint junction is where two walls meet at an angle other than a right angle.

questions.text: Cavity walls
options: Prevent dampness from entering the building
Have lesser dead load for given wall thickness
Are better insulated against heat and sound
questions.expl: Cavity walls offer damp prevention, reduced dead load, and better heat/sound insulation - all benefits.

questions.text: The common thickness used for stone walls in a building is
questions.expl: Stone walls in buildings are commonly constructed about 400 mm thick.

questions.text: Which of the following should be used for hearting of thicker walls?
questions.expl: Headers are used for the hearting (core) of thicker walls to bond through the wall's full thickness.

questions.text: Minimum thickness of wall where single Flemish bond can be used is
options: One and a half bricks thick
questions.expl: Single Flemish bond requires a minimum wall thickness of one and a half bricks.

questions.text: Expansion Joints in masonry walls are provided in wall lengths greater than
questions.expl: Expansion joints are needed in masonry walls once the length exceeds about 40 m.

questions.text: The slenderness ratio for masonry walls should not be more than
questions.expl: The permissible slenderness ratio for masonry walls is limited to 20.

questions.text: Stud(s) of a common wooden partition
options: Is the upper horizontal wooden member
Is the lower horizontal wooden member
Are the intermediate horizontal wooden members
questions.expl: Studs are the vertical wooden members that form the frame of a wooden partition.

questions.text: The exterior angle between outer faces of a wall, is known as
questions.expl: A quoin is the external angle or corner formed between the outer faces of a wall.

questions.text: The entrained concrete is used in lining walls and roofs for making
questions.expl: Air-entrained concrete linings provide both heat and sound insulation to walls and roofs.

questions.text: Expansion joints in masonry walls are provided if length exceeds
questions.expl: Masonry walls need expansion joints once their length exceeds around 40 m.

questions.text: Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The retaining wall should be structurally capable to resist the applied earth pressure
The section of the retaining wall should be so proportioned that it may not overturn by the lateral pressure
The retaining wall should be safe against sliding
To drain off water from the earth retained, weep holes are provided near the top of the retaining wall
questions.expl: Weep holes are actually provided near the bottom, not the top, of a retaining wall, making this statement incorrect.

questions.text: Cavity wall is generally provided for
questions.expl: Cavity walls serve heat insulation, sound insulation, and damp prevention purposes together.

questions.text: Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The width of the wall is constructed thicker at the base in a stepped fashion
A long vertical load transferring concrete structure is called a concrete pile
In pile which transfer the load to the soil by the friction between the pile and the surrounding soil is called friction pile
questions.expl: All the given statements are actually correct, so the answer is none of these being incorrect.

questions.text: For a wall carrying heavy load on low bearing capacity soil,
questions.expl: Heavy walls on weak soil need a thick and reinforced concrete bed to spread the load safely.

questions.text: Herringbone bond is used for
options: Walls having thickness more than 4 bricks
Architectural finish to the face work
questions.expl: Herringbone bond is used in thick walls, decorative facework, and ornamental brick flooring panels alike.

questions.text: A wall constructed to resist the pressure of an earth filling, is called
questions.expl: A retaining wall is built specifically to resist the lateral pressure of earth fill behind it.

questions.text: The range of spread from the wall base to outer edge of a brick work foundation does not exceed
questions.expl: The spread of a brick foundation footing is limited to a maximum of 1 horizontal to 1 vertical.

questions.text: The inner section of a cavity wall, is generally known as
questions.expl: Each of the two parallel walls of a cavity wall, including the inner one, is called a leaf wall.

questions.text: Noggin of a common wooden partition is
questions.expl: A noggin is an intermediate horizontal wooden member fixed between the studs of a partition.

questions.text: Ornamental moulded course placed on the top of a wall, is
questions.expl: A cornice is the ornamental moulded course provided at the top of a wall.

questions.text: To construct a 10 cm thick partition wall, you will prefer
questions.expl: A 10 cm (half-brick) thick partition wall is best built using stretcher bond.

questions.text: The minimum thickness of walls built in cement mortar (1:6) for a single storey building, is
questions.expl: For a single storey building, walls in 1:6 cement mortar are kept at least 20 cm thick.

questions.text: Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: Cavity of a cavity wall should start near ground level
Cavity of a cavity wall should terminate near eaves level of sloping roof
Cavity of a cavity wall should terminate near coping of flat roof with parapet wall
questions.expl: All these placement rules for the cavity's start and termination points in a cavity wall are correct.

questions.text: Which one of the following activities is not correct as applicable to brick corbels
options: The maximum projection of the corbel should not be more than the thickness of the wall
The maximum projection of each corbel course should be limited to a quarter brick at a time
The discontinuous corbels are used to carry heavy concentrated loads
Stretcher bond is generally used for the construction of brick corbel
questions.expl: Stretcher bond is not typically used for corbel construction, making this the incorrect statement.

questions.text: The sill of a common wooden partition is
options: Vertical wooden member on either end
questions.expl: The sill is the lower horizontal wooden member at the base of a partition frame.

questions.text: Brick nogging type of partition wall, is constructed by
options: Laying bricks as stretchers in cement mortar
Laying bricks as headers in cement mortar
Reinforcing brick wall with iron straps
Constructing brick work within a wooden framework
questions.expl: Brick nogging partitions are built by filling brickwork within a supporting wooden frame.

questions.text: The process of filling hollow spaces of walls before plastering, is known
questions.expl: Dubbing out is the process of filling hollow or uneven spaces in a wall before plastering.

questions.text: A wall constructed with stones to protect slopes of cuttings in natural ground from the action of weathering agents, is called
questions.expl: A breast wall is built to protect natural ground slopes from weathering, not to resist earth fill pressure.

questions.text: The width of the hollow space between two walls of a cavity wall should not exceed
questions.expl: The cavity width between the two leaves of a cavity wall should not exceed about 10 cm.

questions.text: The thickness of a reinforced brick partition wall, is generally kept
questions.expl: A reinforced brick partition wall is generally kept about 10 cm thick.

questions.text: Weep holes are provided in retaining and breast walls
options: To drain off the water from the filling
To reduce the weight of the earth retained
questions.expl: Weep holes allow accumulated water behind retaining/breast walls to drain off, relieving hydrostatic pressure.
